comp.notes: Base + equity + benefits; range not captured from posting.

fit.verdict: Bordering. The code + AI-prototyping story is the best-ever fit for a visual role — the JD explicitly wants React front-end prototyping and AI-assisted prototyping, which is exactly him and rare in a visual designer. But it's a Staff role gated on 10+ yrs of deep typography/color/iconography craft plus a mentoring track record — two things the codebase doesn't supply.

criteria.name: 10+ yrs visual design; deep type/color/iconography at product/brand scale
criteria.note: Layout & type pairing yes; a governed product type scale / icon set — not shown. Hard blocker.

criteria.name: Portfolio range: foundational systems + expressive high-craft
criteria.note: Style Registry + format-breakdown docs = foundational; editorial work = expressive.

criteria.name: Conviction + language to articulate what makes design succeed
criteria.note: The craft-breakdown docs are literally this, written down.

criteria.name: Systems thinking: expressive vs. pragmatic for a data-rich product
React front-end prototyping + systems-in-code + AI prototyping
criteria.note: This is him, exactly, heavily substantiated.

strengths: React front-end prototyping + working with engineers on how systems get built in code — rare in a visual designer, and an explicit JD ask
AI-assisted prototyping — production pipelines, not experiments
Craft references documented into repeatable playbooks (what the JD calls 'systems, guidelines, references that make it repeatable')
gaps: No governed product type scale / color system / icon set ownership
Stakeholder influence is client-facing, not design-org-internal

nextAction: Secondary to the Accounting role. If applying, lead hard with the 'designer who codes and ships the system' angle + the format-breakdown/Style-Registry docs as proof of repeatable-craft systems. Acknowledge the type/icon-depth gap honestly.
